ranked_facts.concept_key: firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
ranked_facts.why: The presence of firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk is more characteristic of Eosinophilic Fasciitis and Systemic Sclerosis-related Cutaneous Fibrosis than of Psoriasis or Atopic Dermatitis, and does not strongly support or contrast with Systemic Disorders with Cutaneous Manifestations or Other Cutaneous Disorders.

ranked_facts.concept_key: nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles
ranked_facts.why: The histopathological finding of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles is more typical of Eosinophilic Fasciitis and Systemic Sclerosis-related Cutaneous Fibrosis than of Psoriasis or Atopic Dermatitis, and does not strongly support or contrast with Systemic Disorders with Cutaneous Manifestations or Other Cutaneous Disorders.
